blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

The Condos & Townhomes 0/0 combination is shared by three Langley sub-areas (Campbell Valley, County Line Glen Valley and Otter District), and Otter District and Campbell Valley are the two sub-areas with zero sales in both splits. An Otter District median is not verified — SnapStats publishes medians at community level only.

Where the condo stock concentrates: there is none to concentrate. The board counted zero attached listings in the sub-area in September 2026; the feed's attached-form product is pad-rental park homes, and the rest of the feed is freehold acreages. The structural reason, in one line: much of this district is Agricultural Land Reserve country, and ALR residences cannot be stratified.

Poppy Secondary, 23752 52 Ave, Langley. A school's presence nearby is not a catchment assignment. Poppy Secondary, no middle school shown) belongs to that address only and must not be extended to Otter District homes.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Otter District Guide

items.t: The ALR frame — the governing fact for much of this district: ALR land may generally have no more than one residence per parcel unless it qualifies for an additional residence, and local governments may further regulate or restrict residences through zoning. The principal residence maximum is a total floor area of 500 m²; a secondary suite is permitted only when it is entirely contained within the principal residence (a separate or detached dwelling is not a secondary suite) and local bylaws permit it; and one additional detached residence is permitted without an ALC application at up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha, subject to local bylaws. ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)). Parcel-level ALR status: confirmed on the ALC's ALR maps, not from the sub-area name.

Township zoning and the coach house: rural homes in this part of the Township sit under Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, and the feed's own listings name RU-2 zoning for acreage parcels; zone assignments for a specific parcel come from the bylaw Map Schedules through the Township's GeoSource. In Bylaw 2500, s. 102, a "coach house" is an accessory dwelling unit located only within the second storey of a detached garage — it is a fee-simple second unit under the zoning bylaw, never strata — and no coach-house size cap appears in s. The Township caps a secondary suite at 120 m² maximum gross floor area (Bylaw No. 2500, s. 102 definition).

SSMUH — Township Bylaw 6020, and why it mostly does not reach this district: the bylaw amendments adopted November 18, 2024 (Bylaw 6020) permit SSMUH in residential zones previously restricted to single-family or duplex use, but eligibility requires the property to be within the Urban Containment Boundary, connected to both municipal water and sewer, not larger than 4,050 m² and not in a zone with a minimum lot size larger than 4,050 m²; properties that do not meet those criteria are instead eligible for one residential unit plus one secondary suite or accessory dwelling unit, depending on zoning — the frame most rural Otter acreages fall under. There is no six-unit tier in the Township.

Pad rent (the park): pad rent at Langley Grove Estates is governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act: the rent increase limit for manufactured home site tenancies is 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026 and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027.

items.t: Fee-simple contrast — the district's acreages ARE the fee-simple case: A fee-simple property carries no strata, no Form B, no strata fees — title, Township rules and registered covenants only.

ALR frame — the governing fact for much of this district: on ALR land, one principal residence is permitted without an ALC application at a maximum total floor area of 500 m² (no more than 1,000 m² of fill); a secondary suite is permitted only when entirely contained within the principal residence (a separate or detached dwelling is not a secondary suite) and local bylaws permit it; and one additional detached residence is permitted at up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha, subject to local bylaws. ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)). Two first-page listings state ALR status in their own text (the South Otter Schoolhouse property "within the ALR"; a 5.45-acre parcel "located in the ALR and zoned RU-2") — listing copy for those parcels only, not a district-wide designation.

SSMUH (Township): Zoning Bylaw 6020, adopted November 18, 2024, has no six-unit tier. Township eligibility for SSMUH requires the property to be within the Urban Containment Boundary, connected to both municipal water and sewer, not larger than 4,050 m² and not in a zone with a minimum lot size larger than 4,050 m². Properties that do not meet those criteria are instead eligible for one residential unit plus one secondary suite or accessory dwelling unit, depending on zoning, which is the frame most rural Otter acreages will fall under. The urban SSMUH numbers should not be applied to an acreage.

In Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s. 102, a "coach house" is a fee-simple second unit — an accessory dwelling unit located only within the second storey of a detached garage; never strata, never a townhouse complex. A ground-floor detached suite is a different accessory unit with different rules.

Plans (Township standing frame): the Willoughby Community Plan originates as Bylaw 1836 (1979), now Schedule 6 to Bylaw 6200 (adopted Dec 1, 2025); Willoughby Plan Update Bylaws 6201/6202/6203 had first/second reading May 25, 2026 only, with a Public Hearing directed for June 15, 2026 — adoption/repeal claims are not verified, and any page claiming the Plan was "replaced" by those bylaws is in error.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Otter District

items.t: ALR block (the governing frame for much of this district — parcel status still parcel-specific): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)) — creating a bare-land strata on ALR land is itself a subdivision needing the same permission. ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m² (no more than 1,000 m² of fill), suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha), where municipal bylaws also permit it. Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

Strata block (bare-land strata parcels, if met outside the ALR): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). A fee-simple lot carries none of this.

Farm class is three tiers, not one (BC Assessment). $2,500 of farm income on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line understates the test for small and large parcels alike.

items.t: The governing figure for any home is its own written site tenancy agreement.

faq.a: The attached-form product the feed shows is manufactured homes in one pad-rental park, Langley Grove Estates.
faq.q: Are there any condos in Otter District?

faq.a: Within the ALC frame, one additional detached residence is permitted without an ALC application at up to 90 m² on a property of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on a property over 40 ha, subject to Township bylaws; the principal residence itself is capped at 500 m², and a secondary suite must be entirely inside the principal residence (and within the Township's 120 m² suite cap).
faq.q: Can I build a second house on an Otter District acreage in the ALR?

faq.a: No. Township eligibility for 3–4 units under Bylaw 6020 requires Urban Containment Boundary location, municipal water and sewer, and a lot no larger than 4,050 m², and there is no 6-unit tier in the Township at all; a rural Otter lot that fails those tests falls to one unit plus a suite or accessory unit depending on zoning.
faq.q: Can I use the urban SSMUH numbers on an Otter acreage?

faq.a: No — it is a manufactured-home park at 3665 244 Street (also carded at 24330 Fraser Highway).
faq.q: Is Langley Grove Estates a condo complex?

faq.a: Within the ALC frame, one additional detached residence is permitted without an ALC application at up to 90 m² on a property of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on a property over 40 ha, provided there is only one existing residence when construction begins and Township bylaws allow it; the principal residence itself is capped at 500 m², and a secondary suite must be entirely inside the principal residence.
faq.q: Can I build a second house on an Otter District acreage in the ALR?

faq.a: Not on ALR land within the ALC frame: ALR residences cannot be stratified — a strata plan deposit is a subdivision (SPA s. 239) and subdivision of agricultural land is prohibited unless the Commission permits it (ALCA s. 21(1); ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6).
faq.q: Can I strata-title the second home later?

faq.a: Almost never on this ground: Township SSMUH eligibility requires Urban Containment Boundary location, municipal water and sewer, and a lot no larger than 4,050 m².
faq.q: Can I put 3–4 SSMUH units on an Otter acreage?

faq.a: Only through the Approving Officer under the Land Title Act, to the zone minimums (RU-2 and RU-3 need 8.0 ha for a new lot; RU-1 needs 1.7 ha) — and ALR land also needs Agricultural Land Commission approval to subdivide.
faq.q: Can I subdivide an Otter District acreage?

faq.a: Parcel-level floodplain mapping is not verified for this district.
faq.q: What should I check before closing on an acreage here?

faq.a: The park's own rules beyond individual listing text are not verified.
faq.q: Is a Langley Grove Estates park home an acreage?

faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — the park owns the land, and your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act.
faq.q: In Langley Grove Estates, do I own the land?

faq.a: No. Listings for the park state "no age restrictions" — it is an all-ages manufactured-home community at 24330 Fraser Hwy / 3665 244 St. The clubhouse, exercise centre and sauna/hot tub in its listing text do not make it a seniors park.
